newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Sharif says appeal brings in dollars.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Sharif says appeal brings in dollars.

text.p: Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Wednesday overseas Pakistanis had sent home about $150 million after he appealed to them earlier this month to boost the country's foreign exchange reserves.
Sharif had appealed to Pakistanis to send $1,000 each to Pakistan through legal channels rather than as an illegal bill of exchange called "hundi".

In a brief speech to the National Assembly (lower house) on Wednesday after winning a massive vote of confidence from the 217-seat house, he said there had been a "very effective response" to the appeal made after his Pakistan Muslim League party won a landslide in the February 3 general elections.
He said he had reports that some $150 million sent by overseas Pakistanis since then had arrived in the country.
"It is a revolutionary achievement within days," Sharif said.

Many Pakistanis working abroad send their remittances home through the "hundi" system, which makes quick dilveries to their relations and gives them a more favourable exchange rate than the official rate.
Under this system, Pakistanis working abroad give hard currency to "hundi" operators whose agents in Pakistan deliver the amount in local currency.
Sharif pledged to give a new impetus to the economy, which he said had suffered during the previous three years of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto.

All economic indicators so far, including a rise in the stock market prices and small gains made by the rupee against the dollar, were encouraging and showed the confidence of the business community, he said.
He added he hoped the Pakistani currency would gain more strength.
